cues.en: We've occasionally talked about what it might be like to be the last sentient life standing at the end of time and looking back at your once glorious civilization.
cues.zh: 我们偶尔会聊起，在时间尽头成为最后一个有知觉的生命，回望曾经辉煌的文明，会是怎样的感觉。

cues.en: But what if we spin the time dial even further ahead in time,
cues.zh: 但如果我们把时间拨盘再往前拨，

cues.en: set it all the way past the end of eternity until that last person could not even remember their past civilization?
cues.zh: 一路越过永恒的尽头，直到最后那个人甚至记不起自己过去的文明呢？

cues.en: It's been a year since we did the first episode of the Civilizations at the End of Time series, Black Hole Farming.
cues.zh: 距离我们做《时间尽头的文明》系列第一集《黑洞农场》已经过去一年了。

cues.en: To my surprise, that episode went on to become the most watched one on the channel, so it seems like it deserves a sequel.
cues.zh: 出乎我意料的是，那一集成为了频道里观看量最高的一集，所以它似乎值得一个续集。

cues.en: It probably shouldn't have been too surprising since the end of time and civilization
cues.zh: 这其实也不该太意外，因为时间与文明的终结

cues.en: is something upon which we ponder and speculate quite a lot.
cues.zh: 正是我们经常思考和猜测的话题。

cues.en: It is also the conceptual center of numerous stories both in and out of science fiction.
cues.zh: 它也是众多故事的概念中心，无论科幻内外。

cues.en: The best of these, in my opinion, is the short story The Last Question
cues.zh: 在我看来，其中最好的是短篇小说《最后的问题》，

cues.en: by the Grandmaster of Science Fiction Isaac Asimov.
cues.zh: 出自科幻大师Isaac Asimov之手。

cues.en: Since this episode is sponsored by Audible,
cues.zh: 既然本期节目由Audible赞助，

cues.en: and is our first occasion working with them, we'll spend a little time discussing Asthma near the end, and try to keep it spoiler free, because you can pick up The Last Question by using my link, audible.com/isaac,
cues.zh: 这也是我们第一次与他们合作，我们会在结尾花点时间聊聊Asimov，尽量不剧透，因为你可以通过我的链接audible.com/isaac获取《最后的问题》，

cues.en: or click on the link in the description below. That gets you a free audiobook and a thirty day free trial of Audible.
cues.zh: 或点击下方描述中的链接。这样你就能获得一本免费有声书和Audible的三十天免费试用。

cues.en: The problem with doing a sequel to a video about the End of Time is there's not really supposed to be a sequel, unless you have a time machine.
cues.zh: 给一部讲“时间终结”的视频做续集，问题在于本来就不该有续集——除非你有台时间机器。

cues.en: As I said in that discussion,
cues.zh: 正如我在那次讨论中所说，

cues.en: there are things we could do to keep life going even after the Black Hole Era, but to do that we should first recap some of what we've already discussed last time, then introduce concepts like Boltzmann Brains and the Margolo's Levantine Limit on Quantum Computing and Reversible Computing.
cues.zh: 即使在黑洞时代之后，我们也有办法让生命延续；但要做到这点，得先回顾上次讨论过的一些内容，再引入玻尔兹曼大脑，以及量子计算与可逆计算中的 Margolus-Levitin 极限等概念。

cues.en: We also need to discuss Quantum Tunneling, Proton Decay,
cues.zh: 我们还需要讨论量子隧穿、质子衰变，

cues.en: Iron Stars,
cues.zh: 铁星，

cues.en: and the fate of the Universe itself.
cues.zh: 以及宇宙本身的命运。

cues.en: We'll try to keep the technical aspects to a minimum,
cues.zh: 我们会尽量把技术内容压到最少，

cues.en: but they are there and this is going to be a fairly long episode,
cues.zh: 但它们确实存在，而且这集会相当长，

cues.en: so as always,
cues.zh: 所以和往常一样，

cues.en: it might not be a bad idea to grab a drink and a snack before we start.
cues.zh: 开始前先拿点饮料和零食，可能不是个坏主意。

cues.en: To recap what we explored in the original episode,
cues.zh: 回顾一下原集里探讨的内容，

cues.en: a black hole can be tapped for energy in three principal ways.
cues.zh: 黑洞主要有三种方式可以提取能量。

cues.en: The first and easiest is to drop mass into the thing and capture its kinetic energy as it plummets,
cues.zh: 第一种也最简单：把质量丢进黑洞，并在它下落时捕获其动能，

cues.en: like attaching a rock to a string wrapped around a generator and tossing the rock off the side of a building.
cues.zh: 就像把石头系在绕发电机转的绳子上，然后把石头从楼边扔下去。

cues.en: The second is to use its rotational energy like a big dynamo,
cues.zh: 第二种是像用一台大发电机那样利用它的旋转能，

cues.en: slowing down its spin in exchange for electricity.
cues.zh: 通过减慢它的自转来换取电能。

cues.en: The third method is to tap into the Hawking Radiation they are believed to emit.
cues.zh: 第三种方法是利用黑洞被认为会发出的霍金辐射。

cues.en: For very small black holes, there is actually a much higher amount emitted at a given time than from bigger ones.
cues.zh: 对非常小的黑洞来说，它们在给定时间内发出的辐射量其实比大黑洞高得多。

cues.en: Any black hole gives off a large chunk of its mass energy as Hawking Radiation,
cues.zh: 任何黑洞都会以霍金辐射的形式释放出自身很大一部分质能，

cues.en: but while the big ones have more overall,
cues.zh: 但虽然大黑洞的总量更多，

cues.en: double the mass, double the energy, they give it off far more slowly.
cues.zh: 质量翻倍，能量翻倍，它们释放得却慢得多。

cues.en: If you double the mass, you also quarter the energy it gives off for any given time period.
cues.zh: 如果质量翻倍，你在任意给定时间段内释放的能量反而只剩四分之一。

cues.en: The amount of power is also constantly rising since in the absence of sufficient new material upon which to feed, the black hole's mass shrinks and smaller black holes give off more power.
cues.zh: 功率还会不断上升，因为没有足够的新物质可供吞噬时，黑洞质量会缩小，而更小的黑洞释放功率更高。

cues.en: In an ideal scenario,
cues.zh: 在理想情况下，

cues.en: you would make your own black hole with the power generation rate you wanted and just keep feeding it matter to maintain it at the same level of mass.
cues.zh: 你可以制造一个自己想要的发电功率的黑洞，并持续喂给它物质，把质量维持在同一水平。

cues.en: You could make one that masses about a billion tons, gives off a billion watts of power, a gigawatt,
cues.zh: 你可以造一个约十亿吨重的黑洞，释放十亿瓦功率，也就是一吉瓦，

cues.en: and lives for about a trillion years,
cues.zh: 并存活约一万亿年，

cues.en: giving off that amount of power the whole time.
cues.zh: 全程释放这么多功率。

cues.en: Ideally, you could feed matter into such a black hole indefinitely,
cues.zh: 理想情况下，你可以无限期地往这样的黑洞里喂物质，

cues.en: replacing whatever was burnt off.
cues.zh: 补充被烧掉的部分。

cues.en: That's roughly the power output of our bigger nuclear and hydroelectric
cues.zh: 这大致相当于我们较大的核电站和水电站的

cues.en: plants, and you'd only need to feed about a kilogram of matter per year to keep it going indefinitely.
cues.zh: 功率输出，而且你每年只需喂约一公斤物质，就能让它无限期运转下去。

cues.en: Indefinitely
cues.zh: 无限期

cues.en: is a theoretically incorrect term in this context however,
cues.zh: 然而在这个语境下，从理论上说这个说法并不正确，

cues.en: because the entire galaxy masses out somewhere near ten forty two kilograms,
cues.zh: 因为整个星系的质量大约在 10 的 42 次方公斤左右，

cues.en: enough to feed such a black hole generator for a million million million million million million
cues.zh: 足以供这样一台黑洞发电机运行 10 的 36 次方

cues.en: years.
cues.zh: 年。

cues.en: Not bad, considering humanity's basically been around for a million years, and we will start running out of natural starlight in the Universe in a few million million years.
cues.zh: 考虑到人类存在了大约一百万年，这成绩还不错，而几百万个百万年后，宇宙中将不再有自然的星光。

cues.en: Yet a naturally occurring black hole lives even longer than that and does so by trickling its power out far more slowly.
cues.zh: 然而，自然形成的黑洞寿命比这还要长，而且它以更缓慢的方式释放能量。

cues.en: We discussed harnessing power from such behemoths in the original episode,
cues.zh: 我们在原节目中讨论过如何利用这种庞然大物的能量，

cues.en: by dropping matter into them or tapping their rotational energy,
cues.zh: 通过将物质投入其中或提取它们的旋转能量，

cues.en: but this won't let you get all of their energy.
cues.zh: 但这并不能让你获取它们的全部能量。

cues.en: Whereas a smaller black hole evaporates via Hawking Radiation quite quickly, naturally occurring ones do so at such a slow rate that it could take eons to gather enough power to flip a single switch.
cues.zh: 较小的黑洞会通过霍金辐射迅速蒸发，而自然形成的黑洞蒸发速度极慢，可能需要亿万年才能聚集足够的能量来拨动一个开关。

cues.en: Once you've exhausted all of its rotational energy, which is enormous,
cues.zh: 一旦耗尽其巨大的旋转能量，

cues.en: and dropped in every last bit of spare matter you have, all that's left is that Hawking Radiation.
cues.zh: 并投入你所有剩余的备用物质，剩下的就只有霍金辐射了。

cues.en: However, running an entire civilization
cues.zh: 然而，让整个文明

cues.en: on levels of power that you'd need sensitive equipment to even detect is probably
cues.zh: 依靠需要精密设备才能探测到的能量水平运行，可能

cues.en: impossible.
cues.zh: 是不可能的。

cues.en: Impossible for biological
cues.zh: 至少对生物

cues.en: life anyway.
cues.zh: 生命来说不可能。

cues.en: Once you start abandoning neurons in favor of computer chips, the game changes a lot.
cues.zh: 一旦你开始用计算机芯片取代神经元，游戏规则就大不一样了。

cues.en: Doing so means that now, hypothetically,
cues.zh: 这意味着，在假设情况下，

cues.en: you can take advantage of those longer lived black holes.
cues.zh: 你可以利用那些寿命更长的黑洞。

cues.en: They give off just tiny trickles of power, but it takes a lot less energy to run a computer based human,
cues.zh: 它们只释放微弱的能量，但运行一个基于计算机的人类所需的能量要少得多，

cues.en: and you would also be able to slow down the speed of consciousness.
cues.zh: 而且你还能减慢意识的速度。

cues.en: It doesn't matter if it takes you a trillion years to complete a sentence, when everyone else experiences time just as slowly and the outside universe is a pretty dead and boring place anyways.
cues.zh: 哪怕你花一万亿年才说完一句话，也无所谓，因为其他人同样觉得时间过得很慢，而且外部宇宙本来就是个死寂又无聊的地方。

cues.en: In part, that's what we meant about these being civilizations at the end of time, because our classic view of time starts meaning less and less.
cues.zh: 在某种程度上，这就是我们说这些是时间尽头的文明的意思，因为我们对时间的经典看法正变得越来越没有意义。

cues.en: Right now, time is a pretty constant thing for us that we all experience at more or less the same rate, yet time slows near black holes, so you can move in close them to slow things down too,
cues.zh: 现在，时间对我们来说相当恒定，我们体验它的速度基本一致；但在黑洞附近时间会变慢，所以你可以靠近它们来让一切慢下来，

cues.en: and if you are also tweaking your rate of thinking down to a glacier pace,
cues.zh: 而如果你又把自己的思考速度放慢到冰川般的程度，

cues.en: you are experiencing periods of time long enough for stars to live and die like ticks on a clock.
cues.zh: 你经历的时间段就会长到足以让恒星像钟表滴答一样生灭。

cues.en: This only tells us what we can do when we run out of other power sources though, how to keep going when you run out of stars.
cues.zh: 不过，这仅仅告诉我们：当其他能源耗尽时我们能做什么，当恒星耗尽时如何继续前行。

cues.en: What we explored in the original episode however was something called the Landauer Limit, which demonstrates that the theoretical maximum calculations
cues.zh: 然而，我们在原集里探讨的是一种叫做兰道尔极限的东西，它表明，理论上的最大计算量

cues.en: you can get out of a given amount of energy depends on the temperature.
cues.zh: 你能从一定能量中获得的计算量取决于温度。

cues.en: The colder it is, the more efficient your computers,
cues.zh: 温度越低，计算机的效率就越高，

cues.en: if that is their limit.
cues.zh: 如果这就是它们的极限的话。

cues.en: Half the temperature, double the calculations per joule of energy used.
cues.zh: 温度减半，每焦耳能量能完成的计算量翻倍。

cues.en: This massively changes the dynamic,
cues.zh: 这会极大地改变整个态势，

cues.en: because suddenly you are not striving to survive after the stars have burned out, but intentionally hoarding your energy until after then because you can use it way more efficiently.
cues.zh: 因为突然间，你不再是在恒星燃尽后努力求生，而是有意把能量囤积到那之后，因为那时你可以更高效地使用它。

cues.en: As the Universe expands,
cues.zh: 随着宇宙膨胀，

cues.en: it gets cooler and cooler,
cues.zh: 它会越来越冷，

cues.en: and right now it's about a hundredth the temperature Earth is.
cues.zh: 现在温度大约是地球的百分之一。

cues.en: Meaning a computer out in the void should be able to do a 100 times the calculations
cues.zh: 这意味着，虚空中的一台计算机应该能做100倍的计算，

cues.en: for the same amount of energy as one can here on Earth.
cues.zh: 而消耗的能量和地球上一样多。

cues.en: Quintillions
cues.zh: 百亿亿

cues.en: of years in the future, when the whole Universe is not even a thousandth of that temperature, you get way more processing power,
cues.zh: 年之后，当整个宇宙的温度连那个温度的千分之一都不到时，你能获得多得多的处理能力，

cues.en: or thinking and living, to put it in human terms, per unit of mass or energy.
cues.zh: 或者说，用人类的话讲，每单位质量或能量能支撑更多思考和生存。

cues.en: Entire planets and planetary populations
cues.zh: 整个行星和行星上的人口

cues.en: could be run-in real time
cues.zh: 都可以实时运行，

cues.en: on less energy than it takes to power whatever speakers you are currently listening to me on.
cues.zh: 所需能量比给你现在听我说话的音箱供电还少。

cues.en: So a civilization might gather up all the matter that it can, storing virtually all of it until the temperature drops to whatever the minimum is that they can function on.
cues.zh: 所以一个文明可能会尽可能收集所有物质，几乎全部储存起来，直到温度降到它们能维持运作的最低水平。

cues.en: From a practical standpoint, a given switch in a computer will need a very long time to cool back down after you use it in order to exploit that ultra low temp computing.
cues.zh: 从实际角度看，为了利用超低温计算，计算机中的某个开关用完后需要很长时间才能冷却下来。

cues.en: This actually works out fine since the biggest black holes give off power so slowly that you'd need trillions of years worth to power a light bulb for an instant.
cues.zh: 这其实没问题，因为最大黑洞释放能量极其缓慢，需要数万亿年的能量才能让灯泡亮一瞬。

cues.en: These factors coincide well if we have very durable equipment that requires minimal maintenance,
cues.zh: 如果我们有非常耐用、几乎免维护的设备，这些因素就能很好地契合，

cues.en: since external objective time is almost meaningless in a dark post stellar universe.
cues.zh: 因为在黑暗的、恒星时代之后的宇宙中，外部客观时间几乎毫无意义。

cues.en: Internal subjective time would be everything,
cues.zh: 内在主观时间就是一切，

cues.en: and to the participants things would seem quite normal.
cues.zh: 而对参与者来说，一切会显得相当正常。

cues.en: In such a scenario, the period of time after the stars burn out is no longer some dead place where at best the last remnants of civilization are barely holding out for just a little while longer.
cues.zh: 在这种情景下，恒星燃尽后的时期不再是死寂之地——那里的最好情况，也不过是文明最后残余勉强再撑一小段时间。

cues.en: It could be hosting mega civilizations that would not even notice a trillion years going by in objective time while enjoying trillions of trillions of years of subjective
cues.zh: 它可能承载着巨型文明，这些文明甚至不会注意到客观时间已过去一万亿年，同时却在享受万亿个万亿年的主观

cues.en: time.
cues.zh: 时间。

cues.en: You could basically have a civilization
cues.zh: 你基本上可以拥有一个文明

cues.en: living around a black hole a few kilometers across that dwarfs a full blown Kardashev three Galactic Empire
cues.zh: 它生活在一个直径几公里的黑洞周围，而这个黑洞让一个完全成型的卡尔达舍夫三级银河帝国相形见绌

cues.en: in every possible respect,
cues.zh: 在一切可能的方面，

cues.en: and that also regards the power output of a light bulb in the same way we do the entire Sun.
cues.zh: 并且它看待一个灯泡的功率输出，就像我们看待整个太阳一样。

cues.en: Nor would each of these black holes necessarily host an entire civilization.
cues.zh: 这些黑洞也未必每一个都承载一整个文明。

cues.en: They might opt to run smaller communities at a higher rate of subjective time, networked with other black hole communities to form a civilization.
cues.zh: 它们可能选择以更高的主观时间速率运行较小的社群，并与其他黑洞社群联网，构成一个文明。

cues.en: Time lag for communications between these is not too big a deal, since it might take light a thousand years to reach your nearest neighbor, but that might seem like normal conversational speed to you and them.
cues.zh: 这些社群之间通信的时间延迟不算什么大问题，因为光可能要一千年才能到达你最近的邻居，但对你和他们来说，那可能就像正常的对话速度。

cues.en: A trillion trillion years in the future, you might be around a black hole somewhere chatting with a friend who was the same but thousands or millions of light years away,
cues.zh: 在万亿个万亿年后的未来，你也许正在某处的黑洞旁，和一个朋友聊天，他和你一样，只不过相隔数千或数百万光年，

cues.en: experiencing no more subjective lag between your environments than you do on the phone or in a chat room, presumably sharing some simulated environment.
cues.zh: 你们所在环境之间的主观延迟，不会比你们打电话或在聊天室里时更大，而且大概还共享着某个模拟环境。

cues.en: With subjective time slowed down so much, things like a galaxy spanning spanning internet finally become possible even if you are still bound by the speed of light.
cues.zh: 当主观时间被放慢到这种程度，像横跨星系的互联网这样的事终于成为可能，即使你仍受光速限制。

cues.en: That was what we discussed last time, as a reminder for those who saw that, but it gives us some questions.
cues.zh: 那是我们上次讨论的内容，算是给看过的人提个醒，但它也给我们带来了一些问题。

cues.en: First, how can you possibly maintain your equipment for those kind of timelines
cues.zh: 首先，在那种时间跨度上，你怎么可能维护自己的设备？

cues.en: with virtually no energy, especially if there is proton decay?
cues.zh: 在几乎没有能量可用的情况下，尤其如果还存在质子衰变？

cues.en: Second, what do you do afterwards?
cues.zh: 其次，之后你做什么？

cues.en: Is it all done then or can life go on?
cues.zh: 是一切就此结束，还是生命仍能继续？

cues.en: The answer to second, if you can solve the first, is yes, kind of.
cues.zh: 第二个问题的答案是：如果你能解决第一个问题，那么是，算是吧。

cues.en: The biggest black holes can live almost ten to the one hundredth years.
cues.zh: 最大的黑洞可以存活将近 10 的 100 次方年。

cues.en: If you can somehow support yourself on that near infinitesimal
cues.zh: 如果你能以某种方式靠那近乎无穷小的

cues.en: trickle of power, you will notice it begins to rise near the end, and you will occasionally notice your neighboring civilizations around their own smaller black holes surging up and eventually exploding.
cues.zh: 一缕能量维持自身，你会注意到它在临近结束时开始增强，也会偶尔注意到邻近文明围绕各自较小的黑洞能量激增，并最终爆炸。

cues.en: Near the end of life for any black hole, it will spike up to energy levels that are quite classically visible. For the last month, it will be bright enough to light a whole planet, and in the end, nearly as bright as a star.
cues.zh: 任何黑洞在生命接近尾声时，能量都会飙升到经典意义上相当可见的水平。在最后一个月里，它会亮到足以照亮整个行星，到最后则几乎和恒星一样亮。

cues.en: That's a lot of power to run a last big party off of to say goodbye,
cues.zh: 靠它来办最后一场盛大的告别派对，这能量可不少，

cues.en: more than enough to re simulate our modern civilization
cues.zh: 用来重新模拟我们的现代文明都绰绰有余

cues.en: many trillions of times,
cues.zh: 数万亿次，

cues.en: but it's also a nice chunk of energy to fuel something afterwards.
cues.zh: 但这也是一大块很好的能量，可以为之后的事情供能。

cues.en: That afterwards is our main interest today.
cues.zh: 后面这部分才是我们今天关注的重点。

cues.en: Let's discuss the maintenance issue real quick.
cues.zh: 咱们快速聊聊维护问题。

cues.en: We can't build stuff that lasts more than a few years or decades nowadays,
cues.zh: 如今我们造的东西撑不过几年或几十年，

cues.en: not when it comes to complex machinery,
cues.zh: 涉及复杂机械时更是如此，

cues.en: so trying to build stuff to last trillions of years with little to no maintenance sounds kind of absurd, absurd, and it certainly is in the context of our current technology.
cues.zh: 所以想造出能运行数万亿年、几乎无需维护的东西，听起来挺荒唐的，确实荒唐，以我们目前的技术而言显然如此。

cues.en: I don't want to sugarcoat this problem.
cues.zh: 我不想粉饰这个问题。

cues.en: Yet we can potentially benefit again from slowing down time, real time too, not just subjective time.
cues.zh: 不过我们或许还能从放慢时间中获益，真实时间也行，不只是主观时间。

cues.en: We can slow down subjective time for thinking by just running a computer slower, various decay processes still occur at the same rate,
cues.zh: 我们可以让计算机跑慢一点来放慢思考的主观时间，各种衰变过程仍以相同速率发生，

cues.en: but time slows down as you get closer and closer to a black hole, and for the very largest black holes you can get quite close before being harmed by tidal forces.
cues.zh: 但越靠近黑洞时间就越慢，而对于最大的黑洞，你可以在被潮汐力伤害之前靠得相当近。

cues.en: This lets you slow down the rate at which decay is occurring in chemical, mechanical, electronic,
cues.zh: 这让你能放慢化学、机械、电子，

cues.en: or even biological systems.
cues.zh: 甚至生物系统中的衰变速率。

cues.en: Of course, they are only going slow from an external view.
cues.zh: 当然，从外部视角看它们只是变慢了。

cues.en: In many ways, a black hole is just an implosion taking place in a slowed down region of space so that it takes eons to witness.
cues.zh: 在很多方面，黑洞不过是在空间中被放慢的区域里发生的内爆，以至于要历经万古才能目睹。

cues.en: Again, it's all about subjective time,
cues.zh: 说到底，一切都是关于主观时间，

cues.en: but that's all that truly matters in a dark Universe where not much is happening.
cues.zh: 但在这个没什么事发生的黑暗宇宙里，那才是真正重要的。

cues.en: However, we have another big advantage from that dark and boring Universe.
cues.zh: 不过，那个黑暗又无聊的宇宙还给了我们另一个大优势。

cues.en: Damage and decay tend to be the result of external events,
cues.zh: 损伤和衰变往往是外部事件的结果，

cues.en: and your machinery wouldn't experience a lot of erosion, oxidation,
cues.zh: 而你的机器若存在于冷却到微开尔文的空无之中，就不会经历太多侵蚀、氧化，

cues.en: or decay when it exists in an empty void chilled down to a microkelvin.
cues.zh: 或衰变。

cues.en: You also have trillions of years to figure out how to build stuff for the long term,
cues.zh: 你还有数万亿年的时间来想办法建造长期存在的东西，

cues.en: not to mention all that time to figure out alternatives like jumping into another younger universe or tapping vacuum energy.
cues.zh: 更不用说还有那么多时间去寻找替代方案，比如跳进另一个更年轻的宇宙，或者提取真空能量。

cues.en: You might just flat out learn how to violate energy conservation or tell entropy to take a hike.
cues.zh: 你甚至可能干脆学会如何违反能量守恒，或者让熵滚远点。

cues.en: Solve any of those and you can have civilizations that last a very long time.
cues.zh: 解决其中任何一个问题，你就能拥有持续极长时间的文明。

cues.en: Of course, one big problem with matter is that on these kind of time scales,
cues.zh: 当然，物质的一个大问题是，在这种时间尺度上，

cues.en: just about everything has to be considered unstable
cues.zh: 几乎一切都必须被视为不稳定的

cues.en: and radioactive.
cues.zh: 且具有放射性的。

cues.en: Carbon 14,
or radiocarbon,
cues.zh: 也就是放射性碳，

cues.en: is very handy for radiocarbon dating because it only has a half life of about six thousand years.
cues.zh: 用于放射性碳定年非常方便，因为它的半衰期只有大约六千年。

cues.en: You wouldn't want to build anything out of radiocarbon that you wanted to last millions of years because it will start turning into nitrogen on you.
cues.zh: 你不会想用放射性碳来建造任何需要存在数百万年的东西，因为它会开始变成氮。

cues.en: Many other substances,
cues.zh: 许多其他物质，

cues.en: while we call them stable, still have half lives that are long but not infinite.
cues.zh: 虽然我们称它们为稳定，但仍然有很长但并非无限的半衰期。

cues.en: This is made worse if proton decay occurs,
cues.zh: 如果发生质子衰变，情况会更糟，

cues.en: but if it doesn't, on long enough timelines,
cues.zh: 但如果不发生，在足够长的时间线上，

cues.en: longer than even the black hole era,
cues.zh: 甚至比黑洞时代还长，

cues.en: we do have to worry about all matter turning into iron, which we'll get to later.
cues.zh: 我们确实得担心所有物质都变成铁，这个我们稍后会讲到。

cues.en: Overall though, you just have to worry about slowly losing matter to unavoidable losses,
cues.zh: 不过总的来说，你只需要担心物质因不可避免的损失而缓慢流失，

cues.en: be it collisions or evaporation or decays.
cues.zh: 无论是碰撞、蒸发还是衰变。

cues.en: It's all fixable,
cues.zh: 这些问题都能解决，

cues.en: but you need to be able to do that with virtually no energy, because you have virtually no power.
cues.zh: 但你得几乎不费力就能做到，因为你几乎没有可用的能量。

cues.en: Once again, time slows near black holes, so you might be able to dance around this issue that way too.
cues.zh: 再说一次，黑洞附近时间会变慢，所以你也许能用这个办法绕开这个问题。

cues.en: Now we also have proton decay to consider.
cues.zh: 现在，我们还得考虑质子衰变。

cues.en: Under the standard model, protons last forever,
cues.zh: 在标准模型中，质子永远不会衰变，

cues.en: but in some other models they do decay somewhere in between ten thirty one and ten thirty six years or longer.
cues.zh: 但在其他一些模型中，质子会在十的三十一次方到十的三十六次方年之间，或更久之后衰变。

cues.en: Either of those are a near eternity compared to the stellar epoch of the Universe,
cues.zh: 无论是哪种情况，相比宇宙的恒星时代都近乎永恒，

cues.en: but it's shorter than any naturally occurring black hole would live, even a small one with a dwarf planet's mass instead of a star.
cues.zh: 但还是短于任何自然形成的黑洞的寿命，哪怕是一个质量相当于矮行星、而不是恒星的小黑洞。

cues.en: This doesn't change things too much if our civilization has mastered making black holes they can actually add matter to. They wouldn't be able to use Hawking Radiation from bigger ones because they couldn't exist that long without all their matter decaying and would be limited to just using their rotational energy and artificial smaller black holes.
cues.zh: 如果我们的文明已经掌握了制造黑洞并向其中添加物质的技术，这就不会带来太大影响。他们无法利用较大黑洞的霍金辐射，因为这些黑洞无法在物质全部衰变前存在那么久；他们只能利用黑洞的自转能，以及人工制造的小黑洞。

cues.en: They still operate like any other black hole civilization,
cues.zh: 他们仍然像其他黑洞文明一样运作，

cues.en: except they'd generally be trying to prevent black holes from forming naturally or merging.
cues.zh: 只不过通常会设法阻止黑洞自然形成或彼此合并。

cues.en: We may however be able to make further use of decaying protons,
cues.zh: 不过，我们或许还能进一步利用正在衰变的质子，

cues.en: since protons are assumed to decay into pions that turn into gamma rays,
cues.zh: 因为人们认为质子会衰变成介子，介子又会转变成伽马射线，

cues.en: a nice source of power, and positrons.
cues.zh: 这能提供不错的能量来源，还会产生正电子。

cues.en: The positron is the antiparticle
cues.zh: 正电子是反粒子

cues.en: of the electron,
cues.zh: 即电子的反粒子，

cues.en: and perhaps you could alter everything to run off positronium
cues.zh: 也许你可以改造一切，让它靠电子偶素运转

cues.en: instead. Instead. Positronium
cues.zh: 替代。替代。电子偶素

cues.en: is a quasi atom composed of a positron and an electron orbiting each other, instead of an electron around a proton, as in hydrogen.
cues.zh: 是一种准原子，由正电子和电子互相绕转组成，而不是像氢那样由电子绕质子转。

cues.en: It is perhaps possible to build new types of molecules out of it, allowing you to continue on even with proton decay.
cues.zh: 也许可以用它构建新型分子，让你即使发生质子衰变也能继续存在。

cues.en: In the normal model for the end of the Universe, things keep expanding forever with large clumps of matter bound together by gravity and the rest are carried so far away they eventually redshift over the cosmological
cues.zh: 在宇宙终结的常规模型中，万物永远膨胀，大团物质被引力束缚在一起，其余物质被带到极远处，最终红移越过宇宙学

cues.en: horizon.
cues.zh: 视界。

cues.en: Best guess right now is that our galaxy and its nearest neighbors will eventually merge into one big galaxy that will stay together and that's it. That is, barring artificial intervention of sorts, which we'll get to shortly.
cues.zh: 目前最靠谱的猜测是：我们的星系和最近邻最终会合并成一个大星系，并一直保持在一起，就这样。也就是说，除非有某种人为干预——这个我们稍后会讲到。

cues.en: In this version of things, all matter eventually ends up in black holes, dead stars or objects too small to naturally be either.
cues.zh: 在这种版本中，所有物质最终都会进入黑洞、死星，或小到自然状态下既成不了黑洞也成不了死星的物体。

cues.en: We can live around those dead stars for a very long time too,
cues.zh: 我们也可以围绕那些死星生活很久很久，

cues.en: but they eventually cool down into super dense super cold objects with so much gravity we'd have a hard time mining them usefully.
cues.zh: 但它们最终会冷却成超致密、超低温的天体，引力太强，我们很难有效地开采它们。

cues.en: They will have another use for us later however,
cues.zh: 不过，它们以后对我们还有另一种用途，

cues.en: in the formation of iron stars,
cues.zh: 在于形成铁星，

cues.en: but that takes a very long time even compared to the Black Hole Epoch.
cues.zh: 但即使与黑洞纪元相比，那也需要非常长的时间。

cues.en: We can't be sure we have that much time though, and we have a theory called the Big Rip, which might prevent us from even getting to the Black Hole Epoch, let alone the Iron Star Epoch.
cues.zh: 不过我们无法确定是否有那么多时间，而且我们有一个叫“大撕裂”的理论，它可能让我们连黑洞纪元都到不了，更别说铁星纪元了。

cues.en: We don't know much about what makes the Universe expand,
cues.zh: 我们对宇宙膨胀的成因知之甚少，

cues.en: other than it appears to be accelerating,
cues.zh: 只知道它似乎在加速，

cues.en: which is why we call the force doing this dark energy, we are not illuminated yet on what it is.
cues.zh: 所以我们把推动这一过程的力称为暗能量，目前还不清楚它到底是什么。

cues.en: You will have heard where a
cues.zh: 你可能听说过

cues.en: this accelerated expansion rips the entire Universe to shred in just twenty billion years.
cues.zh: 这种加速膨胀会在短短两百亿年内把整个宇宙撕成碎片。

cues.en: As an FYI,
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，

cues.en: that period was calculated
cues.zh: 那个时间是用

cues.en: using an arbitrary round value for w, the relevant constant, of negative 1.5.
cues.zh: w 的一个随意取整值算出来的，这个相关常数取的是负1.5。

cues.en: We do not know what its value is, just that it's probably negative one or close to it, but if you plug in negative 1.5
cues.zh: 我们不知道它的值是多少，只知道它大概是负一或接近负一，但如果你代入负1.5

cues.en: you get about twenty billion years left, stick in negative one and you get infinity.
cues.zh: 就会得到大约还剩两百亿年，代入负一就会得到无穷大。

cues.en: There is no theory saying the Universe ends in twenty billion years,
cues.zh: 没有理论说宇宙会在两百亿年后终结，

cues.en: it was just an example in the original paper.
cues.zh: 那只是原论文里的一个例子。

cues.en: If it were negative two in the example, it would be ten billion years,
cues.zh: 如果例子里取负二，那就是一百亿年，

cues.en: if it were negative 1.1,
cues.zh: 如果取负1.1，
就是一千亿年。

cues.en: But if this theory is right, and w is not exactly equal to negative one,
cues.zh: 但如果这个理论是对的，而 w 并不正好等于负一，

cues.en: the force acting to expand the Universe would eventually grow strong enough to override the gravitational force existing between all galaxies,
cues.zh: 那么推动宇宙膨胀的力最终会强到压倒所有星系之间的引力，

cues.en: then between all stars,
cues.zh: 接着压倒所有恒星之间的引力，

cues.en: then strong enough to override the gravity holding stars and planets together.
cues.zh: 再强到压倒维系恒星和行星的引力。

cues.en: Taken to its conclusion,
cues.zh: 推演到最后，

cues.en: it finally reaches a level powerful enough to override the electromagnetic
cues.zh: 它最终会达到一种强度，足以压倒电磁

cues.en: forces binding molecules together,
cues.zh: 即把分子束缚在一起的力，

cues.en: and eventually even nuclei themselves.
cues.zh: 最终甚至连原子核本身也能压倒。

cues.en: However, the thing about quarks,
cues.zh: 不过，夸克这种东西，

cues.en: and the strong nuclear force that binds them together,
cues.zh: 以及把它们束缚在一起的强核力，

cues.en: is that when you pull on two quarks to rip them apart, you have to exert so much energy to do that that you actually end up spawning two new pairs of quarks.
cues.zh: 问题在于：当你拉扯两个夸克试图把它们撕开时，必须施加极大的能量，结果反而会生成两对新的夸克。

cues.en: So you get this huge new out point of new matter everywhere.
cues.zh: 于是，到处都会涌出大量新物质。

cues.en: It's a bit of a hydra thing, slice up a quark pair and get two more.
cues.zh: 这有点像九头蛇：切开一对夸克，反而多出两对。

cues.en: That's also one way to convert energy into matter.
cues.zh: 这也是把能量转化为物质的一种方式。

cues.en: The theory gets a bit more uncertain at that point since it operates under general relativity,
cues.zh: 到那时，理论会变得更不确定，因为它建立在广义相对论之上，

cues.en: which is very iffy at the atomic scale,
cues.zh: 而广义相对论在原子尺度上很不可靠，

cues.en: and of course our understanding of dark energy is not terribly precise or ironclad either.
cues.zh: 当然，我们对暗能量的理解也谈不上多精确、多牢靠。

cues.en: Right now it's a bit of a black box.
cues.zh: 目前它还有点像个黑箱。

cues.en: We know what it does but not how it works or where it comes from, and we can't rule out that a better understanding of it might open a new energy source for us. See the Dark Energy episode for more discussion of it.
cues.zh: 我们知道它做什么，却不知道它如何运作、从何而来，也不能排除更深入的理解会为我们打开一种新能源。更多讨论见暗能量那集。

cues.en: Regardless of what happens when you get to the atomic unbinding stage,
cues.zh: 不管进入原子解绑阶段时会发生什么，

cues.en: nothing would be around to witness it so it wouldn't matter to you. If your scientists determine that it is the correct theory,
cues.zh: 都不会有谁留下来见证，所以对你来说也无关紧要。如果你的科学家确定这就是正确理论，

cues.en: you then figure out the actual timeline you have left and ration resources accordingly.
cues.zh: 那你就得算出自己实际还剩多少时间，并据此配给资源。

cues.en: If you've got twenty billion years, you really have no reason to conserve anything.
cues.zh: 如果你有200亿年，你确实没理由节省任何东西。

cues.en: I've heard folks suggest you can make a very large black hole and tuck your civilization in it for protection,
cues.zh: 我听人说，可以造一个超大黑洞，把文明塞进去保护起来，

cues.en: but I've also heard the Big Rip takes out black holes too.
cues.zh: 但我也听说，大撕裂连黑洞也会摧毁。

cues.en: I would say a cosmologist could provide a better answer, but we have no proper theory for quantum gravity, so it's probably a guessing game right now anyway.
cues.zh: 我会说宇宙学家能给出更好的答案，但我们还没有合适的量子引力理论，所以目前大概只能靠猜。

cues.en: That end expansion is very fast too, so you wouldn't duck inside a black hole to buy a little more time or anything.
cues.zh: 那种终末膨胀也非常快，所以你不会躲进黑洞去多争取一点时间什么的。

cues.en: Assuming the Big Rip isn't the case though, civilizations looking at real long term solutions probably want to conserve matter and energy as much as they can, and probably hoard it from wherever they can.
cues.zh: 不过，假设大撕裂不会发生，寻求真正长期方案的文明大概会尽可能保存物质和能量，并尽可能到处囤积。

cues.en: It stands to reason that if you are planning to keep your civilization around as long as you can,
cues.zh: 按理说，如果你打算让自己的文明存续得尽可能久，

cues.en: you will start hoarding matter so that it doesn't get burnt up uselessly in stars or fall into black holes bigger than you want or get ejected out of the galaxy.
cues.zh: 你就会开始囤积物质，免得它在恒星中白白烧掉、掉进过大的黑洞，或被抛出星系。

cues.en: This is one of the reasons we say in the Dyson Dilemma that civilizations
cues.zh: 这也是我们在《戴森困境》中说的一点：文明

cues.en: that don't want to expand their numbers might seem to expand anyway,
cues.zh: 即使不想扩大数量，也似乎仍在扩张，

cues.en: as they journey outwards not to colonize other solar systems but to stockpile their matter instead,
cues.zh: 它们向外迁移，不是为了殖民其他恒星系，而是为了囤积物质，

cues.en: like squirrels holding nuts because winter is coming.
cues.zh: 就像松鼠囤坚果，因为冬天要来了。

cues.en: Big stars do make valuable heavy elements,
cues.zh: 大质量恒星确实会制造有价值的重元素，

cues.en: but supernovae
cues.zh: 但超新星

cues.en: are not efficient methods for that, and odds are civilizations that want more of those would prefer to use a giant particle accelerator instead,
cues.zh: 并不是高效的方法，而且想要更多这类元素的文明，很可能更愿意用巨型粒子加速器，

cues.en: as we discussed in last week's Dyson Spheres episode.
cues.zh: 正如我们上周戴森球那期节目里讨论的。

cues.en: I also mentioned there that it is possible to move planets or stars.
cues.zh: 我在那里也提到过，移动行星或恒星是可能的。

cues.en: However, it is also possible to move galaxies.
cues.zh: 不过，移动星系也是可能的。

cues.en: In all of these cases, the method is not high-tech,
cues.zh: 在所有这些情况中，方法并不高科技，

cues.en: just very big.
cues.zh: 只是非常庞大。

cues.en: The Great Wall or Pyramids were huge tasks, but hardly high-tech.
cues.zh: 长城或金字塔是巨大的工程，但算不上高科技。

cues.en: While technology can possibly make it much easier to do or offer you other methods,
cues.zh: 虽然技术可能让事情容易得多，或者提供其他方法，

cues.en: Fundamentally,
cues.zh: 但根本上，

cues.en: it is not complicated,
cues.zh: 并不复杂，

cues.en: just an application of the maxim, if brute force isn't working, you're not using enough of it.
cues.zh: 只是应用一条格言：如果蛮力不起作用，说明你用得还不够多。

cues.en: If you don't mind waiting a billion years,
cues.zh: 如果你不介意等上十亿年，

cues.en: you can place a ton of thin mirrors near a star and have them bounce the light in one direction,
cues.zh: 你可以在恒星附近放置大量薄镜子，让它们把光反射到一个方向，

cues.en: accelerating them up to quite high speeds,
cues.zh: 将其加速到相当高的速度，

cues.en: as explained in the Shkadov's Thruster episode.
cues.zh: 正如《Shkadov推进器》那一集所解释的。

cues.en: You can accelerate that process by using methods we discussed in Star Lifting to spew out increased amounts of solar wind, like a rocket engine flame.

cues.zh: 另一种可能是，

cues.zh: 铁星甚至可能更早变成黑洞，只需区区 10 的（10 的 26 次方）年，然后你重启自身。

cues.en: That black hole that forms, being of less than one solar mass,
cues.zh: 形成的那个黑洞，质量不到一个太阳质量，

cues.en: will once more give off only a tiny trickle of energy, but it would seem like a banquet feast compared to what you were used to back in the black hole epoch.
cues.zh: 将再次只释放涓涓细流般的能量，但比起你在黑洞纪元习惯的，那简直像一场盛宴。

cues.en: Finally though, it will end, after another near eternal golden age.
cues.zh: 不过最终，在又一个近乎永恒的黄金时代之后，它还是会结束。

cues.en: It slowly rises in power until it gives off its last gas,
cues.zh: 它的功率会慢慢攀升，直到释放出最后的气体，

cues.en: shining nearly as brightly as the stars that disappeared so long ago.
cues.zh: 绽放出几乎与很久以前熄灭的群星同样耀眼的光芒。

cues.en: And then that is essentially it.
cues.zh: 到这里，一切基本就结束了。

cues.en: If you haven't figured out how to keep going in the face of entropy by now, it is too late.
cues.zh: 如果你到现在还没想出在熵增面前活下去的办法，那就太迟了。

cues.en: But you will get that final second black hole epoch, or neutron star epoch, depending on how the physics of that works out.
cues.zh: 但你确实能迎来那最后的黑洞纪元，或是中子星纪元，这取决于物理定律究竟如何运作。

cues.en: And yet,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: it is not necessarily
cues.zh: 这并不一定

cues.en: the end of intelligence,
cues.zh: 是智慧的终结，

cues.en: even if it is the end of civilization.
cues.zh: 哪怕它意味着文明的末日。

cues.en: If matter is required to store information,
cues.zh: 如果存储信息必须依赖物质，

cues.en: and you've been accumulating so much of it, you've probably also been discarding extra bits to keep going a while longer.
cues.zh: 而你积攒了那么多物质，那你大概也会不断丢弃多余的比特，好让自己多苟延残喘一会儿。

cues.en: If the Sun went out, you could stay alive a while longer by tossing your furniture and books into the fireplace,
cues.zh: 如果太阳熄灭了，你可以把家具和书本扔进壁炉里取暖，多活上一阵子，

cues.en: and while you might not be able to bring yourself to toss your favorite book into the fire to buy a few more minutes, all sorts of old manuals and reference books might find themselves in there.
cues.zh: 即便你狠不下心把最喜欢的书扔进火里换取几分钟，各种陈旧的手册和参考资料大概也免不了被丢进去。

cues.en: Odds are pretty good such civilizations
cues.zh: 很有可能，这样的文明

cues.en: would do the same, maybe trading every memory for a little more time, maybe just old tax returns and astronomical tables
cues.zh: 也会采取同样的做法，或许是用每一段记忆去换取多一点点时间，或许只是把泛黄的税单和天文星表

cues.en: sacrificed to live a while longer.
cues.zh: 牺牲掉，来换取多活片刻。

cues.en: In the end, they go, sooner rather than later if they want to keep a lot, but they can keep some in reserve almost to the end, because the power levels will rise for a black hole near the end, or for the collapse of an iron star to a neutron star.
cues.zh: 最终它们都难逃消亡；如果想保留很多记忆，消亡得还会更快，但它们几乎可以把一部分保留到最后，因为在黑洞走向终局、或是铁星坍缩为中子星时，功率水平都会骤然升高。

cues.en: Either way, this is when time,
cues.zh: 不管怎样，到了这个时候，时间

cues.en: as any meaningful measure, has truly come to an end. Eternity has come and gone and taken with it any civilizations
cues.zh: 作为任何有意义的度量，都真正走到了尽头。永恒来去匆匆，带走了一切文明

cues.en: and their records.
cues.zh: 以及它们的记载。

cues.en: But again,
cues.zh: 但话说回来，

cues.en: not necessarily intelligence.
cues.zh: 智慧却未必就此终结。

cues.en: We call it the heat death of the Universe even though it is terribly cold, because everything is in thermal equilibrium,
cues.zh: 虽然那里极度寒冷，我们仍称之为宇宙的“热寂”，因为万物都处于热平衡，

cues.en: there is no longer any source for energy.
cues.zh: 不再有任何能量来源。

cues.en: Entropy and the laws of thermodynamics
cues.zh: 熵和热力学定律

cues.en: have finally closed the book on things.
cues.zh: 终于为万物画上了句号。

cues.en: Yet inside that random chaos, it is possible for occasional bits of order to emerge.
cues.zh: 然而在那片随机的混沌中，偶尔也有可能浮现出一丝秩序。

cues.en: If I take a deck of cards and put it in order, then shuffle it, it becomes disordered,
cues.zh: 如果我把一副扑克牌按顺序理好，然后洗牌，它就会变得混乱，

cues.en: more and more every time I shuffle it. But if I do that enough times,
cues.zh: 每洗一次就更混乱一分。但如果洗的次数足够多，

cues.en: it will return to its original state.
cues.zh: 它终究会回到最初的状态。

cues.en: It could happen at any time,
cues.zh: 这随时都可能发生，

cues.en: but on average, for a 52 card deck,
cues.zh: 但平均来说，对于一副 52 张的扑克牌，

cues.en: it should take approximately 52 factorial shuffles,
cues.zh: 大约需要洗 52 的阶乘次，

cues.en: or 52 times 51 times 50 times 49,
cues.zh: 也就是 52 乘 51 乘 50 乘 49，

cues.en: etc, all the way down to one.
cues.zh: 以此类推，一直乘到 1。

cues.en: In this case, if I shuffled that deck once every second,
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，如果我每秒洗一次牌，

cues.en: I should expect to reset it in about ten to the sixtieth years.
cues.zh: 预计要花大约 10 的 60 次方年才能复原。

cues.en: This may seem an impossibly long time period,
cues.zh: 这听起来像是一段不可思议的漫长时间，

cues.en: but on the timelines we've been looking at today,
cues.zh: 但放到我们今天探讨的时间尺度来看，

cues.en: that's actually rather modest.
cues.zh: 其实已经相当短暂了。

cues.en: Were I to use only one suit of cards, just 13 cards, in order from ace to king, That would be more like two hundred years,
cues.zh: 如果我只用同一种花色、从 A 到 K 仅仅 13 张牌，那就只需要大约两百年，

cues.en: something which you might see in your own lifetime of shuffling.
cues.zh: 这甚至是你一生不停洗牌真有可能见证的奇迹。

cues.en: Likewise, if I used a larger deck, it would take far longer.
cues.zh: 同样，如果我用一副更大的牌，耗时会长得多。

cues.en: Back in Ludwig Boltzmann's day, we knew about entropy,
cues.zh: 回到路德维希·玻尔兹曼的时代，我们已经了解熵，

cues.en: but thought the Universe was steady state.
cues.zh: 但当时认为宇宙处于稳态。

cues.en: In a closed system like that, no matter how big it is, just like shuffling a deck of enormous cards,
cues.zh: 在那样一个封闭系统中，无论它有多大，就像洗一副巨大的牌，

cues.en: eventually your particles all reset,
cues.zh: 最终你的粒子都会重置，

cues.en: and will reset to something close enough far sooner.
cues.zh: 而且会更快地重置到足够接近的状态。

cues.en: When all this chaos and random action,
cues.zh: 当所有这些混沌和随机运动，

cues.en: even processes which normally build up entropy,
cues.zh: 甚至那些通常会增加熵的过程，

cues.en: become effectively reversible,
cues.zh: 实际上变得可逆，

cues.en: so long as there is a finite chance of them occurring.
cues.zh: 只要它们有有限的发生概率。

cues.en: And in the Infinite Improbabilities episode,
cues.zh: 而在《无限不可能性》那一集中，

cues.en: we discussed all the weird things that can happen when we begin giving incredibly tiny yet still finite odds
cues.zh: 我们讨论了当我们开始赋予极其微小但仍有限的概率，

cues.en: near infinite time or space to work in.
cues.zh: 并给予近乎无限的时间或空间来运作时，可能发生的各种奇怪事情。

cues.en: One of those weird things is the Boltzmann Brain,
cues.zh: 其中一件奇怪的事情就是玻尔兹曼大脑，

cues.en: that even in a Universe reduced to total entropy, out of that chaos will emerge a random pattern of matter that is a thinking creature.
cues.zh: 即使在一个熵达到最大值的宇宙中，从混沌中也会随机涌现出一种物质模式，那是一个有思维的生物。

cues.en: Everything is bumping around chaotically
cues.zh: 一切都在混沌中碰撞

cues.en: and just happens to create a random pattern that is, for instance,
cues.zh: 恰好形成了一个随机模式，比如，

cues.en: a big sentient supercomputer
cues.zh: 一台有感知的大型超级计算机，

cues.en: with a nice nuclear reactor attached to it to run it until the components or fuel decays.
cues.zh: 还配有一个不错的核反应堆来驱动它，直到组件或燃料衰变。

cues.en: Perhaps even a nice habitat with plants inside it, with a person to eat them, a little Eden if you will.
cues.zh: 甚至可能是一个不错的栖息地，里面有植物，有人来吃它们，可以说是小小的伊甸园。

cues.en: After eternity in this frigid random soup,
cues.zh: 在这冰冷的随机汤中度过永恒之后，

cues.en: these minds could just keep popping up. We do not live in a steady state universe, ours is expanding,
cues.zh: 这些心智可能会不断涌现。我们并不生活在稳态宇宙中，我们的宇宙在膨胀，

cues.en: so we are pretty much guaranteed no total resets of entropy,
cues.zh: 所以我们基本上可以保证不会出现熵的完全重置，

cues.en: but Boltzmann Brains can exist and indeed can come to be in other Universes where the physical constants might have values that normally preclude life or even simple chemistry, from occurring.
cues.zh: 但玻尔兹曼大脑可以存在，而且确实可以在其他宇宙中产生，那里的物理常数可能具有通常阻止生命甚至简单化学发生的值。

cues.en: Indeed in some Universes they'd probably be the only kind of life that could exist.
cues.zh: 在有些宇宙里，它们大概会是唯一可能存在的生命形式。

cues.en: Over an infinite period of time, anything that can happen will happen,
cues.zh: 在无限长的时间里，任何可能发生的事都会发生，

cues.en: including a stable and long lasting Boltzmann Brain,
cues.zh: 包括一个稳定而长久的玻尔兹曼大脑，

cues.en: which might sit around contemplating ways to deal with entropy.
cues.zh: 它可能闲坐着思考应对熵的方法。

cues.en: Such an entity would not remember us though. It would not know or remember that there ever was a Universe beyond the frozen sea of chaos all around it,
cues.zh: 不过这样的实体不会记得我们。它不会知道或记得，在它周围那片冰封的混沌之海以外，曾经存在过一个宇宙，

cues.en: but it would be alive and thinking.
cues.zh: 但它会活着，并且在思考。

cues.en: And since, if one could exist,
cues.zh: 而且，既然一个都可能存在，

cues.en: there is an even smaller chance two could exist near each other in time or space,
cues.zh: 两个在时间或空间上彼此靠近存在的概率就更小，

cues.en: or three or more, we do have a chance for a civilization
cues.zh: 三个或更多就更小；但我们确实有机会出现一个文明

cues.en: after the end of time.
cues.zh: 在时间终结之后。

cues.en: And you only need a chance.
cues.zh: 而你只需要一个机会。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: is as far as we go looking into the future, so while we might do some more episodes on civilizations
cues.zh: 就是我们向未来眺望的极限；所以虽然我们可能还会做几集关于文明的节目

cues.en: at the end of time, there have to be prequels, not sequels.
cues.zh: 讲时间终结时的文明，但那必须是前传，而不是续集。

cues.en: Time can't really be said to have an end, and in a lot of ways we aren't talking about the end of time but our general fight against entropy itself.
cues.zh: 其实很难说时间会有终点；从很多方面说，我们谈的不是时间的终结，而是我们对抗熵本身的总体战争。

cues.en: It's a long drawn out war, with a lot of battles along the way, even before the death of our own Sun, which as we've seen in this series,
cues.zh: 这是一场旷日持久的战争，沿途有许多战斗，甚至在我们自己的太阳死亡之前也是如此；而正如本系列所见，

cues.en: is more of a prologue than epilogue to civilization.
cues.zh: 太阳之死更像是文明的前传，而不是尾声。

cues.zh: 我在开头提到过，这集献给阿西莫夫和他的短篇小说《最后的问题》，

cues.en: which is focused on that theme and is generally voted his best short story.
cues.zh: 它聚焦于这个主题，通常被评为阿西莫夫最好的短篇。

cues.zh: 还出现在五六本Asmo短篇小说选集中。

cues.zh: 甚至六十年后，这个故事对计算机和未来的谈论方式依然惊人地准确，
